summary.headline: SG Finserve posted an all-time high quarterly PAT of INR59 crore in Q2 FY27, with loan book at ~INR5,700 crore and H1 PBT of INR150 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported record Q2 FY27 PAT of INR59 crore and a loan book of about INR5,700 crore, up roughly 25% QoQ on period-end basis (average AUM up 17% QoQ). Asset-to-equity rose from 2.8x to 3.7x over the last year, and quarterly ROE reached about 15%. Management revised its mid-term debt-to-equity ceiling from 3x to 4x, which it said would take AUM to about INR11,000 crore, and it expects no equity raise this year. New initiatives during the quarter included factoring/TReDS, digital lending, loan against property (LAP), and a stake in an AI/digital subsidiary, plus a GIFT City subsidiary and an AIF pending SEBI approval.

segments.name: Supply chain finance (dealer / deep-tier)
segments.commentary: Supply chain is ~70% of AUM. Group ecosystem share of book has fallen to 25%; the company powers ~60 brands. Steel and building products ~35% of AUM and auto ~20%.

segments.name: Factoring / TReDS
segments.commentary: Factoring licence received in March 2026; now ~15% of book after starting in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Digital lending (BharatPe merchant LSP model)
segments.commentary: ~10,000 loans disbursed; book only INR121 crore at 30 Sep 2026. Management expects ~10% of AUM in 2-3 years.

segments.name: Loan against property (LAP) / business loans
segments.commentary: Just started in Delhi NCR with four disbursals and INR17 crore outstanding; tickets above INR25 lakh.

segments.name: Project finance
segments.commentary: 12 accounts disbursed recently, none commercially operational; management expects starts in 6-9 months.

guidance_outlook: Debt-to-equity mid-term ceiling revised from 3x to 4x; board approved incremental borrowing in the call's board meeting.
AUM growth guidance of 30-35% CAGR on a one-year-forward basis; profitability CAGR guidance of 35-40%.
Management targets INR10,000-11,000 crore AUM in 2-3 years, implying ~100% growth from current book; equity dilution or higher leverage mandate expected only after that.
Full-year PAT guidance of INR225 crore reiterated; management said it may do slightly better.
Expects around 7,000 crore AUM by year end on current run rate (per management comment); Q2/Q4 seasonality of 2-3% on the higher side.
Target of adding 2 anchor corporates per month for the next 12-18 months.
GIFT City finance subsidiary (~INR48 crore investment approved) expected operational in about a year, subject to RBI and IFSCA approvals.
Planning to keep ROA above 4.5% and cost-to-income below 15%; yield maintained at ~13% on AUM.
capex_capacity: Headcount ~100 (roughly doubled in one year); per-employee annualised PAT above INR2 crore; presence in 34 locations.
Digital lending built on LSP framework; in-house AI/digital stack being built via a 15% stake in a subsidiary rather than external SaaS.
New subsidiaries: AIF (Cat III equity AIF, SEBI approval awaited), AMC subsidiary, GIFT City finance company (~INR48 crore), shared services company (cost amount undecided), AI/technology subsidiary.
Project finance: 12 accounts, none yet operational.
LAP: specialist team hired; scaling to be gradual, starting in Delhi NCR.
demand_pricing: Wallet share across the ~60 anchor brands is under 5%; management targets doubling to 10%, plus 20-25 new brands in the next year.
~800 active customers, average ticket ~INR7 crore; per-borrower appetite limited.
Yield on AUM maintained at ~13% (ROI ~12.5% plus 50-70 bps fee income); range 11-15% by risk category.
Lending rates are benchmarked to the SGFL benchmark rate; management said any repo-linked cost increase would be passed on, though benchmark not yet raised.
Management positions the company as filling the INR10-20 'untied' portion of borrowers' funding need after banks/NBFCs.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company raise equity this financial year, given borrowings near 3x net worth?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Debt-to-equity mandate raised to 4x, with incremental borrowing approved by the board; equity dilution or higher leverage considered 2-3 years out.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue grow ~18% QoQ while AUM grew 25%?
qa_highlights.answer: Income accrues on daily outstanding; average AUM grew 17% QoQ, so period-end growth overstates income growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest cost as a percentage of income rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher leverage (asset-to-equity 2.8x to 3.7x); management said this lifts ROE.

qa_highlights.question: What is the collection efficiency and DPD profile?
qa_highlights.answer: Monthly collection efficiency 99.5%; 60+ DPD is zero overall and 30+ DPD is zero in non-supply-chain book; 0.5% slips to 1+ DPD and is mostly collected within 30 DPD.

qa_highlights.question: How does the RBI draft on revolving credit affect the model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the product is term-based with no rollover or extension, so it is aligned; only documentation and reporting systems need tweaks.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost of funds and funding mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Single source is banks and NBFCs (19 lenders), plus opportunistic commercial paper; cost of borrowing about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Q2 credit cost increase a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Provisioning is an ECL/IRAC regulatory requirement, not cash credit cost; ~INR25 crore accumulated on ~INR5,700 crore book, and nil NPA is the target.

qa_highlights.question: Why would borrowers choose SG over banks?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowers often get INR80-90 of a INR100 requirement from banks; SG funds the remaining untied portion, under a coexistence model across PSU banks, private banks, large NBFCs and mid-layer NBFCs.

risks_watch: Leverage rising toward the 4x D/E ceiling; equity dilution likely around INR10,000-11,000 crore AUM given the ~3x price-to-book; watch the CCD/OCD option.
Finance cost ratio rising (44.5% of interest income); repo hike and benchmark pass-through timing unclear.
Draft RBI norms on revolving credit could require documentation and system changes for supply-chain products (about two-thirds of AUM).
BharatPe digital-lending book: management acknowledged gross NPAs are possible, relying on FLDG and LSP cushions.
New businesses (AIF, GIFT City, LAP, project finance) carry execution and gestation risk; project finance accounts not yet operational.
Management said the Q2 front-loading of growth may normalise; the 30-35% growth guide must be tested in H2.
Opex discipline as headcount and locations expand; the cost-to-income target is below 15%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and leverage, with repeated emphasis on conservatism. Management was evasive on digital-lending ROA ('will not be able to divulge the commercials') and on the cost and timing of the shared-services company and the AIF, and it was cautious on the RBI draft, calling it a documentation tweak.
key_quotes: Our mid-term target was to not leverage ourselves beyond debt-to-equity of 3x. But now considering the growth which has front-loaded, we are revising our leverage to debt-to-equity of 4x.
Our collection efficiency, Mayank, is 99.5% on a month-on-month basis.
The objective is to not increase the cost; our objective is to bring synergy and reduce the cost or worst, maintain the cost.
So the problem is not the TAM; the problem is, what we want to do and what we don't want to do, because as I said, we are a very conservative lender.
